newsitem.title: UK: P&O shares sink on MMC referral for Stena JV.
newsitem.headline: P&O shares sink on MMC referral for Stena JV.

text.p: Shares in Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co sank on Thursday on news the British government would refer the ferry group's proposed joint venture with Sweden's Stena Line to competition authorities.

P&O shares traded around 594p prior to the news but then dropped sharply to a low of 574-3/4p before recovering to 587p by 1134 GMT, down nine pence on the day. Some 566,000 shares had changed hands by that time.
The referral to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) for investigation follows plans unveiled last month for P&O and Stena to join forces on three English Channel routes.

The planned merger was designed to rationalise the two shipping lines' capacity on the busy short-sea route where the English Channel is at its narrowest and competition with the Channel tunnel most fierce.
James Halstead, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing in London said the referral decision was slightly unexpected and disappointing for the market.

"They were effectively given the green light in summer by the Government when the injunction on a merger was removed and the Government saw the impact on business after the Channel tunnel opened. We thought there would be no problem," he said.
Halstead said he did not expect the P&O share to fall further and called the initial reaction overdone.
"The MMC has to report within three months, which gives the ferries ample time to get ready for the summer season which is where the real returns lie," he added.
A second analyst, who asked not to be named, suggested there could be political concerns behind the referral, given Eurotunnel's problems with the recent fire.
"This could well be a political move...there is some political sensitivity with the fire," the analyst said.
